extraFacts.fact: Stainless Steel Heat Exchanger Tubes (Indus listing /p/stainless-steel-heat-exchanger-tubes): TP304/304L, TP316/316L, TP321, TP347, duplex; 15.88 to 31.75 mm OD; sizes from 0.889 to 2.769 mm wall.
Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless Tubes (Indus listing): TP405, TP409, TP410, TP430, TP439, 26-3-3; feedwater heaters (TP439 under A803).

faqs.q: What are extra-long stainless steel tubes used for?
faqs.a: The Extra-Long Stainless Steel Tubes are single straight or developed lengths up to 30 m, for long exchangers and feedwater heaters where a joint in the tube is not acceptable. Long tubes cut the number of joints and allow fewer, longer bundles.

faqs.q: How do I specify the Extra-Long Stainless Steel Tubes, since there is no fixed size table?
faqs.a: They are made to your drawing, so the size table is a set of limits, not part numbers: send the standard and grade, the OD and wall (BWG or millimetres, minimum or average wall), the length and the quantity. The OD and wall follow the same stainless tube standards as normal-length tube.

faqs.q: What is the longest stainless heat exchanger tube you can supply?
faqs.a: The longest single straight or developed length offered is 30 m; some mills list 22 m or 18 m maximum. Lengths over the usual 12 m need planning for handling, straightness and shipping, and we confirm the length tolerance, straightness and crating with the quotation.

faqs.q: What OD and wall ranges apply to extra-long stainless tubes?
faqs.a: Standard geometry by mill runs from 12–88.9 mm OD with 0.8–4.4 mm wall (European mill) to 12–88.9 mm OD with 0.6–6.0 mm wall (Indian mill), at up to 30 m. These are the limits of the standard, and each item is made to your drawing.

faqs.q: What length tolerance applies to the Extra-Long Stainless Steel Tubes?
faqs.a: Above 7.3 m, ASTM A1016 and A688 allow +3 mm/−0 up to 7.3 m, plus 3 mm per extra 3 m, capped at +13 mm. We confirm the length tolerance and straightness for your length with the quotation.

faqs.q: Which stainless grades are available for the Extra-Long Stainless Steel Tubes?
faqs.a: The Extra-Long Stainless Steel Tubes are listed in TP304/304L, TP316/316L and duplex. Tell us the grade and standard on the enquiry; equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN and JIS are checked against each tender, as [our DIN, EN and ASTM tube equivalents guide](/blog/din-17175-din-1629-en-10216-equivalents) explains.

faqs.q: Which standards and certificates apply to the Extra-Long Stainless Steel Tubes?
faqs.a: The Extra-Long Stainless Steel Tubes are listed to ASTM A213, A269, A789, A1016, A312 and A511, DIN 17456, EN 10216-5 and JIS G3459. A mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request, and third-party inspection can be arranged.

faqs.q: Where are the Extra-Long Stainless Steel Tubes used?
faqs.a: They are used in long-tube exchangers and U-tube bundles where a 30 m developed length avoids butt welds. For bent tubes see the [stainless U-bend tubes](/c/stainless-u-bend-tubes), and for normal lengths the [Stainless Steel Heat Exchanger Tubes](/p/stainless-steel-heat-exchanger-tubes).

faqs.q: How are the Extra-Long Stainless Steel Tubes handled and shipped?
faqs.a: Lengths over the usual 12 m need planning for handling, straightness and shipping, so crating and support are agreed with the quotation. Send the delivery point and any container or road limit on the enquiry.

faqs.q: How do the Extra-Long Stainless Steel Tubes differ from standard-length stainless tubes?
faqs.a: The OD and wall follow the same standards as the [Stainless Steel Heat Exchanger Tubes](/p/stainless-steel-heat-exchanger-tubes), but the length reaches 30 m instead of the usual 12 m. Choose extra-long where a butt weld in the tube is not acceptable.

faqs.q: Can you export the Extra-Long Stainless Steel Tubes from Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes. We ship Extra-Long Stainless Steel Tubes from Dubai, UAE to buyers across the GCC, Africa, Asia and beyond. Long tubes are crated for shipping, as agreed with the quotation. Give the destination and quantity on [our contact page](/contact) and we quote the freight lane with the goods.

faqs.q: Do you keep the Extra-Long Stainless Steel Tubes in stock in Dubai?
faqs.a: Extra-Long Stainless Steel Tubes is quoted from Dubai, UAE against your drawing or data sheet rather than held as a standard item. Lengths up to 30 m are made to your drawing. Send the details through [our contact page](/contact) and we confirm the lead time with the quotation.

faqs.q: What are ferritic and martensitic stainless tubes used for?
faqs.a: The Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless Tubes to ASTM A268, including TP405, TP410 and super-ferritic grades, are used in heat exchangers where chloride stress-corrosion cracking rules out the austenitic grades. A typical service is feedwater heaters in TP439 under A803.

faqs.q: How are the part numbers such as IH-TF-SS-FER-0190-165 read?
faqs.a: IH-TF-SS-FER-0190-165 is the 19.05 mm (3/4 in) OD tube with a 1.65 mm wall, 16 BWG; the other row is the 25.4 mm (1 in) tube with a 2.11 mm wall, 14 BWG. The size table lists these two sizes, and any size inside the range is made to order.

faqs.q: What sizes do the Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless Tubes come in?
faqs.a: The size table lists 19.05 and 25.40 mm OD with 1.65 and 2.11 mm walls. Any size within 19.05–25.4 mm OD and 1.65–2.11 mm wall is made on request; send the OD, wall, length and quantity on the enquiry.

faqs.q: What tolerances does ASTM A268 set for ferritic stainless tube?
faqs.a: A268 allows OD ±0.13 mm below 38.1 mm and ±0.25 mm from 38.1 to 88.9 mm, with wall ±15 % below 12.7 mm OD and ±10 % above, and cut length +3/−0 mm up to 7.3 m. Flattening, flare, hardness and tension tests follow A268 and A1016.

faqs.q: What strength does super-ferritic S44660 (26-3-3) reach?
faqs.a: Super-ferritic S44660 (26-3-3) lists a tensile strength of 585 MPa and a yield of 450 MPa, with 20 % elongation and a hardness limit of 265 HBW or 25 HRC. These are the figures in the listing for that grade; confirm the grade and temper on the enquiry.

faqs.q: Which grades are available in the Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless Tubes?
faqs.a: The Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless Tubes are listed in TP405, TP409, TP410, TP430, TP439 and 26-3-3. TP410 and S41500 are hardenable, high-chromium ferritics can be prone to notch brittleness on slow cooling, and TP439 is used for hot-water tanks without post-weld heat treatment.

faqs.q: Which standards and certificates apply to the Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless Tubes?
faqs.a: The Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless Tubes are listed to ASTM A268 / ASME SA-268, ASTM A803 and DIN 17456. A mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request, and third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan.

faqs.q: What do the Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless Tubes connect to in a feedwater heater?
faqs.a: They are rolled or welded into tube sheets drilled to your drawing; see the [tube sheets](/c/tube-sheets) and, for bent tubes, the [Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless U-Bend Tubes](/p/ferritic-and-martensitic-stainless-u-bend-tubes). [Our stainless heat exchanger tube grades guide](/blog/stainless-heat-exchanger-tube-grades) compares the stainless tube grades.

faqs.q: What heat treatment applies to the Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless Tubes after forming?
faqs.a: ASTM A268 calls for reheating to 650 °C (1200 °F) or higher and cooling as suited to the grade, and S41500 at 510 °C (950 °F) or higher. Hydrostatic or electric non-destructive testing follows A1016.

faqs.q: How do the Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless Tubes differ from austenitic stainless heat exchanger tubes?
faqs.a: These are chosen where chloride stress-corrosion cracking rules out austenitic grades, while the [Stainless Steel Heat Exchanger Tubes](/p/stainless-steel-heat-exchanger-tubes) cover TP304 to TP347 and duplex in 15.88–31.75 mm OD. Pick the grade from the service and confirm it on the enquiry.

faqs.q: Can you export the Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless Tubes from Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes. We ship Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless Tubes from Dubai, UAE to buyers across the GCC, Africa, Asia and beyond. Tubes ship with their mill certificates. Give the destination and quantity on [our contact page](/contact) and we quote the freight lane with the goods.

faqs.q: Is the Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless Tubes available from Indus Hydraulics in Dubai, and what is the lead time?
faqs.a: The Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless Tubes is built to order and supplied from Dubai, UAE, with shipping worldwide. The lead time is confirmed on the quotation. Send the size, rating and quantity through [our contact page](/contact) and we confirm the build and delivery date.

faqs.q: What are stainless steel heat exchanger tubes used for?
faqs.a: The Stainless Steel Heat Exchanger Tubes are seamless and welded austenitic tubes in TP304, 304L, 316, 316L, 321 and 347, with duplex to ASTM A789, for heat exchangers, condensers and feedwater heaters. They are ordered by outside diameter and BWG wall, as minimum or average wall.

faqs.q: How do I read the Indus part numbers such as IH-TF-SS-AUS-0159-089?
faqs.a: IH-TF-SS-AUS-0159-089 is the 15.88 mm OD tube with a 0.889 mm wall (20 BWG): the first group is the OD in tenths of a millimetre and the second the wall in thousandths. The size table lists 23 sizes from 15.88 to 31.75 mm OD, each under its own part number.

faqs.q: Which outside diameters and BWG walls do stainless steel heat exchanger tubes come in?
faqs.a: The size table runs 15.88–31.75 mm OD: 5/8, 3/4, 7/8, 1 and 1-1/4 in, with BWG walls 20, 18, 16, 14 and 12 (0.889 to 2.769 mm). The most-requested sizes are 19.05 × 1.65, 19.05 × 2.11, 25.4 × 1.65 and 25.4 × 2.11 mm; other sizes are made on request.

faqs.q: How do I order stainless heat exchanger tube: minimum wall or average wall?
faqs.a: Tube is ordered by OD and BWG wall, as minimum or average wall, so state which on the enquiry. BWG converts to millimetres as 20 = 0.89, 18 = 1.24, 16 = 1.65, 14 = 2.11, 12 = 2.77 and 10 = 3.40 mm; ASTM A789 duplex tube is supplied on average wall unless minimum wall is ordered.

faqs.q: What tolerances and test pressure apply to the Stainless Steel Heat Exchanger Tubes?
faqs.a: For cold-finished tube under 25.4 mm OD, ASTM A1016 allows +0.10/−0.11 mm on OD, and the hydrostatic test pressure is P = 220.6 × t/D MPa, with 7 MPa the most that need be applied, held for at least 5 s. An electric non-destructive test (eddy current or ultrasonic) may replace the hydro test.

faqs.q: Which stainless grades are available for these heat exchanger tubes?
faqs.a: The Stainless Steel Heat Exchanger Tubes are listed in TP304/304L, TP316/316L, TP321, TP347 and duplex S31803, S32205 and S32750. The listing points to duplex or super duplex for crude/vacuum overhead condensers and chloride cooling water, and 317L or 316L with at least 2.5 % Mo for naphthenic-acid service; see [our stainless heat exchanger tube grades guide](/blog/stainless-heat-exchanger-tube-grades).

faqs.q: Which standards and certificates apply to the Stainless Steel Heat Exchanger Tubes?
faqs.a: The Stainless Steel Heat Exchanger Tubes are listed to ASTM A213 / ASME SA-213, A269, A249 / SA-249, A312, A789, A790 and A1016, and BS 3059. A mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request, and third-party inspection can be arranged; [our DIN, EN and ASTM tube equivalents guide](/blog/din-17175-din-1629-en-10216-equivalents) and [our guide to EN 10204 3.1 mill test certificates](/blog/en-10204-3-1-mill-test-certificate) explain the equivalents and the certificate.

faqs.q: What do I use with the Stainless Steel Heat Exchanger Tubes in an exchanger?
faqs.a: The tubes go into tube sheets drilled to your drawing, and bend to U-tubes where the bundle needs them: see the [stainless U-bend tubes](/c/stainless-u-bend-tubes) and the other tube shelves such as [carbon steel boiler and heat exchanger tubes](/c/carbon-steel-boiler-heat-exchanger-tubes) and [alloy steel boiler and superheater tubes](/c/alloy-steel-boiler-superheater-tubes). Exchanger parts for the bundle are on the [tube sheets shelf](/c/tube-sheets).

faqs.q: How are the Stainless Steel Heat Exchanger Tubes tested and treated after forming?
faqs.a: ASTM A213, A269 and A249 300-series tube is solution annealed at 1040 °C (1900 °F) minimum and water quenched, with maximum hardness of 192 HBW for TP304, 304L, 316, 316L, 321 and 347. A249 welded tube adds reverse-bend and flange tests, and a weld-decay test (S7) is optional.

faqs.q: How do austenitic tubes compare with ferritic and martensitic stainless tubes?
faqs.a: Austenitic tubes (TP304 to TP347) are the general choice, while the [Ferritic and Martensitic Stainless Tubes](/p/ferritic-and-martensitic-stainless-tubes) to ASTM A268 are used where chloride stress-corrosion cracking rules out austenitic grades, such as feedwater heaters in TP439. For very long runs see the [Extra-Long Stainless Steel Tubes](/p/extra-long-stainless-steel-tubes).

faqs.q: Can you export the Stainless Steel Heat Exchanger Tubes from Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes. We ship Stainless Steel Heat Exchanger Tubes from Dubai, UAE to buyers across the GCC, Africa, Asia and beyond. Tubes ship with their mill certificates. Give the destination and quantity on [our contact page](/contact) and we quote the freight lane with the goods.

faqs.a: Yes. We keep Stainless Steel Heat Exchanger Tubes in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and ship worldwide with the best lead times. Send the part numbers and quantities through [our contact page](/contact) for a quotation.
